tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

The call ends your run, so do everything else first and put everything your caller needs in that one report. It is not a messaging channel: do not use it for progress updates or questions.

Only a report delivered through SubagentHandback reaches your caller; plain text you write at the end of your run is NOT delivered. There is no recipient parameter: the report can only go to your caller.

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks.    332	  async function* reviewAttempt(

   359	          'review',
   360	          combineSignals(request.signal, controller.signal),

   363	        prompt: parts.prompt,
   364	        output: Output.array({ element: reviewEditSchema }),
   365	        onError: ({ error }) => {

   376	          firstSuggestionSinceStartMs ??= Math.round(clock() - overallStartMs)

   379	            edit: step.outcome.edit,
   380	            elapsedMs: Math.round(clock() - overallStartMs),
   381	          }
   382	        } else {

   384	          yield {
   385	            type: 'dropped',

   388	          }

   398	        task,
   399	        number,
   400	        failure: completed

   403	        firstElementMs,
   404	        firstSuggestionMs,
   405	      })
   406	    }

   408	      accepted,
   409	      dropped,
   410	      firstSuggestionSinceStartMs: firstSuggestionSinceStartMs ?? null,
   411	      failure,
   412	    }
   413	  }

   415	  async function* reviewDocument(

   421	    const retry =
   422	      first.failure !== undefined &&
   423	      first.accepted === 0 &&
   424	      isRetryableOutputError(first.failure)

   431	    }

   433	      type: 'done',
   434	      accepted: last.accepted,
   435	      dropped: last.dropped,
   436	      attempts: retry ? 2 : 1,
   437	      incomplete: last.failure !== undefined,
   438	      firstSuggestionMs: last.firstSuggestionSinceStartMs,

   486	export type TelemetryCollector = {

   490	    requestedModel: string,

   495	const requestIdOf = (event: unknown): string | undefined => {
   496	  if (typeof event !== 'object' || event === null) return undefined
   497	  const parsed = requestIdSchema.safeParse(
   498	    (event as { runtimeContext?: unknown }).runtimeContext,
   499	  )
   500	  return parsed.success ? parsed.data.requestId : undefined
   501	}
   502	
   503	const callIdOf = (event: unknown): string | undefined =>
   504	  typeof event === 'object' && event !== null
   505	    ? ((event as { callId?: unknown }).callId as string | undefined)
   506	    : undefined
   507	
   508	const errorMessageOf = (event: unknown): string => {
   509	  const error =
   510	    typeof event === 'object' && event !== null
   511	      ? (event as { error?: unknown }).error
   512	      : undefined
   513	  return error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error ?? 'unknown')
   514	}

   516	const complete = (entry: Entry): CallObservation => ({
   517	  ...entry.observation,
   518	  requestedModel: entry.requestedModel,
   519	})

   521	export const createTelemetryCollector = (
   522	  graceMs = DEFAULT_GRACE_MS,
   523	): TelemetryCollector => {
   524	  const entries = new Map<string, Entry>()
   525	  const requestByCall = new Map<string, string>()
   526	
   527	  const update = (
   528	    requestId: string | undefined,
   529	    patch: Partial<CallObservation>,
   530	    finish = false,
   531	  ): void => {
   532	    const entry = requestId === undefined ? undefined : entries.get(requestId)
   533	    if (requestId === undefined || entry === undefined) return
   534	    const next: Entry = {
   535	      ...entry,
   536	      observation: { ...entry.observation, ...patch },
   537	    }
   538	    if (finish) next.settle(complete(next))
   539	    else entries.set(requestId, next)
   540	  }
   541	
   542	  const integration: Telemetry = {
   543	    onStart: (event) => {
   544	      const requestId = requestIdOf(event)
   545	      if (requestId === undefined) return
   546	      requestByCall.set(event.callId, requestId)
   547	    },
   548	    onLanguageModelCallEnd: (event) => {
   549	      const metadata = openRouterMetadataSchema.safeParse(
   550	        event.providerMetadata?.openrouter,
   551	      )
   552	      const openRouter = metadata.success ? metadata.data : undefined
   553	      update(requestByCall.get(event.callId), {
   554	        servedModel: event.modelId,
   555	        finishReason: event.finishReason,
   556	        responseId: event.responseId,
   557	        ...(openRouter?.provider ? { provider: openRouter.provider } : {}),
   558	        ...(openRouter?.usage?.cost === undefined
   559	          ? {}
   560	          : { costUsd: openRouter.usage.cost }),
   561	        ...(event.usage.inputTokens === undefined
   562	          ? {}
   563	          : { inputTokens: event.usage.inputTokens }),
   564	        ...(event.usage.outputTokens === undefined
   565	          ? {}
   566	          : { outputTokens: event.usage.outputTokens }),
   567	        ...(event.usage.outputTokenDetails.reasoningTokens === undefined
   568	          ? {}
   569	          : {
   570	              reasoningTokens: event.usage.outputTokenDetails.reasoningTokens,
   571	            }),
   572	        ...(event.usage.inputTokenDetails.cacheReadTokens === undefined
   573	          ? {}
   574	          : { cachedTokens: event.usage.inputTokenDetails.cacheReadTokens }),
   575	      })
   576	    },
   577	    onEnd: (event) => {
   578	      update(requestByCall.get(event.callId), {}, true)
   579	      requestByCall.delete(event.callId)
   580	    },
   581	    onAbort: (event) => {
   582	      update(requestByCall.get(event.callId), { error: 'aborted' }, true)
   583	      requestByCall.delete(event.callId)
   584	    },
   585	    onError: (event) => {
   586	      const callId = callIdOf(event)
   587	      if (callId === undefined) return
   588	      update(requestByCall.get(callId), { error: errorMessageOf(event) }, true)
   589	      requestByCall.delete(callId)
   590	    },
   591	  }
   592	
   593	  const expect = (
   594	    requestId: string,
   595	    requestedModel: string,
   596	  ): Promise<CallObservation> =>
   597	    new Promise((resolve) => {
   598	      let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined
   599	      const settle = (observation: CallObservation): void => {
   600	        clearTimeout(timer)
   601	        entries.delete(requestId)
   602	        resolve(observation)
   603	      }
   604	      const startGrace = (): void => {
   605	        clearTimeout(timer)
   606	        timer = setTimeout(() => {
   607	          const entry = entries.get(requestId)
   608	          settle(entry ? complete(entry) : { requestedModel })
   609	        }, graceMs)
   610	      }
   611	      entries.set(requestId, {
   612	        requestedModel,
   613	        observation: {},
   614	        settle,
   615	        startGrace,
   616	      })
   617	    })
   618	
   619	  const release = (requestId: string): void => {
   620	    entries.get(requestId)?.startGrace()
   621	  }
   622	
   623	  return { integration, expect, release }
   624	}

   187	export const initialReviewState: ReviewValidationState = {

   192	const dropReason = (
   193	  occupied: ReadonlySet<string>,
   194	  state: ReviewValidationState,
   195	  edit: ReviewEdit,
   196	  block: Block | undefined,
   197	): DropReason | undefined => {
   198	  if (block === undefined) return 'unknown-block'
   199	  if (block.kind === 'code') return 'code-block'
   200	  if (occupied.has(block.id)) return 'occupied'
   201	  if (state.seen.has(block.id)) return 'duplicate-block'
   202	  const replacement = edit.replacement.trim()
   203	  if (replacement === '') return 'empty'
   204	  if (replacement === block.text.trim()) return 'unchanged'
   205	  if (state.accepted >= MAX_REVIEW_EDITS) return 'over-limit'
   206	  return undefined
   207	}

   209	export const acceptReviewEdit = (
   210	  context: ReviewValidationContext,
   211	  state: ReviewValidationState,
   212	  edit: ReviewEdit,
   213	): {
   214	  readonly state: ReviewValidationState
   215	  readonly outcome: ReviewOutcome
   216	} => {
   217	  const block = context.blocks.find(
   218	    (candidate) => candidate.id === edit.blockId,
   219	  )
   220	  const reason = dropReason(context.occupied, state, edit, block)
   221	  if (reason !== undefined || block === undefined) {
   222	    return {
   223	      state,
   224	      outcome: { type: 'dropped', edit, reason: reason ?? 'unknown-block' },
   225	    }
   226	  }
   227	  return {
   228	    state: {
   229	      accepted: state.accepted + 1,
   230	      seen: new Set([...state.seen, block.id]),
   231	    },
   232	    outcome: { type: 'accepted', edit: { ...edit, block } },
   233	  }
   234	}

   236	export const validateReviewEdits = (
   237	  edits: readonly ReviewEdit[],
   238	  blocks: readonly Block[],
   239	  occupied: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(),
   240	): {
   241	  readonly accepted: readonly AcceptedEdit[]
   242	  readonly dropped: readonly DroppedEdit[]
   243	} => {
   244	  const context = { blocks, occupied }
   245	  const accepted: AcceptedEdit[] = []
   246	  const dropped: DroppedEdit[] = []
   247	  let state = initialReviewState
   248	  for (const edit of edits) {
   249	    const step = acceptReviewEdit(context, state, edit)
   250	    state = step.state
   251	    if (step.outcome.type === 'accepted') accepted.push(step.outcome.edit)
   252	    else dropped.push({ edit: step.outcome.edit, reason: step.outcome.reason })
   253	  }
   254	  return { accepted, dropped }
   255	}

   444	export const findBlockAt = (
   445	  blocks: readonly Block[],
   446	  position: number,
   447	): Block | undefined =>
   448	  blocks.find((block) => block.from <= position && position <= block.to)

   450	const distanceTo = (block: Block, position: number): number =>
   451	  position < block.from ? block.from - position : position - block.to

   453	const nearestBlock = (
   454	  blocks: readonly Block[],
   455	  position: number,
   456	): Block | undefined =>

   458	    (best, block) =>
   459	      best === undefined ||
   460	      distanceTo(block, position) < distanceTo(best, position)

   462	        : best,

   466	export const headingText = (block: Block): string => {

   475	  block.from < to && block.to > from

   477	const resolveSelectionTarget = (
   478	  blocks: readonly Block[],
   479	  text: string,
   480	  { from, to }: Selection,
   481	): Target | undefined => {
   482	  const selected = text.slice(from, to)
   483	  if (selected.trim() === '') return undefined
   484	  return {
   485	    source: 'selection',
   486	    from,
   487	    to,
   488	    text: selected,
   489	    blocks: blocks.filter((block) => overlaps(block, from, to)),
   490	  }
   491	}

   493	const resolveCursorTarget = (
   494	  blocks: readonly Block[],
   495	  position: number,
   496	): Target | undefined => {
   497	  const block = findBlockAt(blocks, position) ?? nearestBlock(blocks, position)
   498	  return block === undefined
   499	    ? undefined
   500	    : {
   501	        source: 'block',
   502	        from: block.from,
   503	        to: block.to,
   504	        text: block.text,
   505	        blocks: [block],

   509	export const resolveTarget = (
   510	  blocks: readonly Block[],
   511	  text: string,
   512	  selection: Selection,
   513	): Target | undefined => {
   514	  const from = Math.max(0, Math.min(selection.from, selection.to))
   515	  const to = Math.min(text.length, Math.max(selection.from, selection.to))
   516	  return from === to
   517	    ? resolveCursorTarget(blocks, from)
   518	    : resolveSelectionTarget(blocks, text, { from, to })

   523	  to: Math.max(target.to, ...target.blocks.map((block) => block.to)),
   524	})

   528	  target: Target,

   542	  }

   235	const attemptOnce = async (
   236	  fetchFn: typeof fetch,
   237	  url: string,
   238	  apiKey: string,
   239	): Promise<OpenRouterGeneration | undefined> => {
   240	  try {
   241	    const response = await fetchFn(url, {

   243	    })
   244	    if (!response.ok) return undefined
   245	    const parsed = generationSchema.safeParse(await response.json())
   246	    return parsed.success ? parsed.data.data : undefined
   247	  } catch {

   252	export const fetchGeneration = async ({
   253	  baseURL,
   254	  apiKey,
   255	  id,
   256	  fetch: fetchFn = fetch,
   257	  initialDelayMs = DEFAULT_GENERATION_INITIAL_DELAY_MS,
   258	  delaysMs = DEFAULT_GENERATION_DELAYS_MS,
   259	  sleep = defaultSleep,
   260	}: FetchGenerationOptions): Promise<OpenRouterGeneration | undefined> => {
   261	  if (id === undefined) return undefined
   262	  const url = `${baseURL}/generation?id=${encodeURIComponent(id)}`
   263	  if (initialDelayMs > 0) await sleep(initialDelayMs)
   264	  for (let attempt = 0; attempt <= delaysMs.length; attempt += 1) {
   265	    const generation = await attemptOnce(fetchFn, url, apiKey)
   266	    if (generation) return generation
   267	    const delay = delaysMs[attempt]
   268	    if (delay !== undefined) await sleep(delay)
   269	  }
   270	  return undefined

=== 0002
# 0002. Structured model output; the app owns the anchors

- Status: Accepted (2026-10-28)
- Source: planning session, Q10, Q39

## Context

What can go wrong with a model's answer here:

| Failure | Plain text | Structured JSON |
|---|---|---|
| Wrapper chatter ("Sure! Here's…", code fences) | happens, needs cleaning | gone, the schema enforces the shape |
| Changes beyond the Instruction | happens | happens equally |
| Invented content | happens | happens equally |
| Wrong location (quotes text that doesn't exist) | impossible, the app knows the range | **new risk**, if the model picks the location |

The diff itself guards against rows 2 and 3: every change is visible before Accept. Structure removes row 1 and makes the answer checkable, but can create row 4.

## Decision

- **Strict structured outputs:** `structured_outputs` with OpenRouter `provider.require_parameters: true`, so only providers that support it are used. One zod schema per shape is both the validator and the source of the JSON Schema.
- **Target requests and Refine:** the app already knows the range. The model returns `{ replacement, rationale }`.
- **Review pass:** the app numbers Blocks (`p1`, `p2`, …) before sending. The model returns `{ edits: [{ blockId, replacement, rationale }] }` and never copies text to say where. A Block is a top-level node of the Markdown syntax tree; a whole list is one Block.
- **App-side validation:** drop an item when `replacement` equals the original or `blockId` is unknown. On invalid output, retry once silently, then show an error card.

## Consequences

- No chatter, a Rationale for every change, and answers the app can check.
- Review pass granularity is one Block: two changes in one paragraph become one Suggestion, and a long list is a single Suggestion.
- Format constraints may slightly lower writing quality ("Let Me Speak Freely?", 2024). The Bake-off watches for it ([0010](0010-model-bakeoff.md)).

## Alternatives considered

- **Plain-text Replacement for Target requests:** simplest, but no Rationale and no validation.
- **Quote-anchored edits `{ quote, replacement }` everywhere:** uniform, but a one-character slip in `quote` drops the edit, even where the app already knew the range.
- **Character offsets:** models are bad at counting characters.
- **Blank-line splitting for Blocks:** breaks on lists without blank lines and on code blocks that contain empty lines.
=== 0006
# 0006. Context window and prompt rules

- Status: Accepted (2026-10-28)
- Source: planning session, Q18, Q26, Q27

## Context

A rewrite that ignores the surrounding tone feels pasted in. Sending the whole Document on every request costs more and invites the model to wander.

## Decision

- **Target requests and Refine:** send the Target, its Neighbors (2 Blocks before, 2 after, the document title and the current section heading, ~300–800 tokens), and the Instruction. Refine also sends the original text, previous Instructions and the latest Replacement.
- **Review pass:** send the whole Document with numbered Blocks (it must choose where to act).
- **Fixed prompt rules:**
  1. Answer in the Target's language.
  2. Change only what the Instruction needs.
  3. Do not invent facts, numbers or names.
  4. Preserve Markdown syntax (lists, links, emphasis).
  5. Rationale: one short sentence, in the Document's language.
- **Reasoning:** off or low for Quick actions, where the model allows it.

## Consequences

- Cheaper than sending the whole Document, and the Neighbors carry the tone.
- The model can miss consistency issues outside the Neighbors. That is what the Review pass is for.
- Rule 2 makes the AI timid on open Instructions like "make this better". Free text still allows big changes when the user asks for them.

## Alternatives considered

- **Target only:** cheapest, but blind to tone and topic.
- **Whole Document on every request:** best tone match, but more tokens. A size limit for huge Documents would also be needed (backlog).
=== 0007
# 0007. Suggestion lifecycle

- Status: Accepted (2026-10-28)
- Source: planning session, Q13, Q19, Q20, Q21, Q22, Q25, Q32

## Context

Suggestions are overlays ([0001](0001-inline-overlay-suggestions.md)) and the user keeps typing while they are open or in flight.

## Decision

- **Edits outside a Suggestion:** its range is mapped through the change (CodeMirror `ChangeSet` mapping).
- **Edits inside an open Suggestion, or inside an in-flight request's Target:** Discard it, with a discreet notice ("Suggestion discarded: the text changed").
- **Overlaps:** a new request over an open Suggestion replaces it, so the last one wins. The Review pass skips Blocks with open Suggestions.
- **Active Suggestion:** shows the Accept / Reject / Refine toolbar. Its Rationale shows on hover, and when the text cursor is inside it (keyboard users can't hover). Other Suggestions show only the inline diff.
- **Keys, with the cursor inside a Suggestion:** `Cmd/Ctrl+Enter` Accepts, `Esc` Rejects. Accept is a normal edit, so `Cmd+Z` undoes it. Reject is not undoable in v1. A Review pass also offers Accept all and Reject all.
- **Refine:** a follow-up Instruction on the Active Suggestion. The new Replacement replaces the old one in place. The diff is always against the original text. History stays in memory, with no version arrows in v1.
- **Persistence:** only the Document text goes to `localStorage`. Open Suggestions are lost on reload.
- **Failures:**
  - Missing key: banner ([0005](0005-local-only-vite-proxy.md)).
  - Failed call (network, `402` out of credit, `429`): the Suggestion becomes an error card with Retry. `402` gets its own message.
  - Invalid output: one silent retry, then the error card.
  - Timeout: 30 s.

## Consequences

- Simple, honest rules. A user who bumps into a Suggestion loses it, and can ask again.
- An accidental `Esc` loses a Suggestion. An undoable Reject is in the backlog.

## Alternatives considered

- **Keep a stale Suggestion with "regenerate":** an extra state, and an old diff can't be drawn over changed text.
- **Lock the range while a Suggestion is open:** takes control away from the user.
- **Block new requests until the old Suggestion is resolved:** friction.
- **Allow overlapping Suggestions:** accepting one breaks the other.
- **Rationale always visible, or in a side panel:** the side panel drifts toward the chatbot sidebar.
=== 0008
# 0008. Stream only where each piece arrives validated

- Status: Accepted (2026-10-28)
- Source: planning session, Q24, Q31

## Context

Streaming has three costs here: parsing half-finished JSON, a diff that jitters while text arrives (not-yet-rewritten original text shows as deleted), and showing text before it is validated.

AI SDK v7, verified in its docs on 2026-10-28:
- With `Output.object`, `partialOutputStream` yields partial objects that "cannot be validated against your provided schema". Only the final output is validated.
- With `Output.array`, `elementStream` yields each element "complete and validated against your element schema".

## Decision

- **Review pass:** stream with `Output.array` and `elementStream`. Each Suggestion appears once it is schema-validated by the SDK and checked by the app (`blockId` exists, Replacement differs from the original).
- **Target requests and Refine:** not streamed. `Output.object`, validated before anything is shown.
- **Reopen rule:** if the chosen model's median latency for Target requests is above ~3 s, add a Draft preview: streamed text without a diff that turns into the diff once validated.

## Consequences

- The slowest call, the Review pass, shows its first Suggestion early, with no validation trade-off.
- Target requests stay simple: one state, validated before display.
- The Draft preview sits in the backlog behind a measurable rule.

## Alternatives considered

- **No streaming at all:** simplest, but the Review pass waits for all 6 Suggestions.
- **Stream everything, including a Draft for Target requests:** matches the challenge's "live preview" idea, but adds a visual state and a Draft that can fail validation and vanish.
=== 0009
# 0009. AI SDK v7 instead of plain fetch

- Status: Accepted (2026-10-28)
- Source: planning session, Q31 (web-verified on 2026-10-28)

## Context

Without streaming, plain `fetch` + zod was ~60–80 lines and fully transparent. With validated element streaming ([0008](0008-validated-streaming-only.md)) and per-call records ([AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md#ai-call-records)), the SDK pays for itself.

Facts at decision time:
- `ai@7.0.155` (7.0.0 released 2026-06-25) and `@openrouter/ai-sdk-provider@3.1.0`, which targets `ai@^7`. Both are ESM-only and require Node 22+.
- Telemetry in v7 is a pluggable integration (`registerTelemetry`). A custom integration receives lifecycle events (`onStart`, `onStepEnd` with `usage`, `onEnd`, …) without OpenTelemetry.
- Every OpenRouter response includes `usage` with `cost`, reasoning tokens and cached tokens. `GET /api/v1/generation?id=…` adds `latency`, `generation_time`, `provider_name`, native token counts and more.

## Decision

- Use `ai@^7` + `@openrouter/ai-sdk-provider@^3` + `zod`.
- The provider uses `baseURL` = `${location.origin}/api/openrouter` and a placeholder key. The proxy injects the real key.
- AI call records come from a custom `registerTelemetry` integration plus the generation endpoint.
- `scripts/bakeoff.ts` uses the same client in Node with the real key, so the Bake-off tests the code the app runs.
- Agents follow `.claude/skills/use-ai-sdk` and never write SDK code from memory.

## Consequences

- Element streaming with validation, lifecycle hooks for records, and a cheap path to Draft streaming later.
- Two more dependencies. Node 22+ goes in the README.
- Official recipes run the SDK on a server. We run it in the browser. The core uses `fetch`, and a Chrome article shows `streamText()` working in the browser.
- **Risk:** the provider README does not document `Output.object` or `json_schema`. Slice 2 must verify this. The fallback is `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` (not yet verified).

## Alternatives considered

- **Plain `fetch` + zod:** smallest and transparent, but no validated element streaming.
- **OpenTelemetry export:** from the browser it needs a vendor key in the bundle, or a server.
- **AI SDK DevTools:** stores data in a local JSON file, so it only works in Node. Usable for the Bake-off only.
=== 0010
# 0010. Choose the model by Bake-off

- Status: **Proposed**. Decided at Gate A ([docs/PLAN.md](../../PLAN.md#gates)).
- Source: planning session, Q23, Q33

## Context

On 2026-10-28, from OpenRouter's public API. Prices are US$ per million tokens. Cost per call assumes ~3k input and ~500 output tokens (a Review pass).

| Tier | Model | Origin | Input | Output | ~Cost/call | Providers |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cheap | `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` | US | 0.10 | 0.50 | 0.0006 | 10 |
| Cheap | `openai/gpt-6-luna` | US | 0.10 | 0.50 | 0.0006 | 7 |
| Cheap | `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` | CN | 0.14 | 0.42 | 0.0006 | 41 |
| Cheap | `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` | CN | 0.15 | 0.50 | 0.0007 | 38 |
| Cheap | `qwen/qwen3.8-flash` | CN | 0.15 | 0.47 | 0.0007 | 2 |
| Cheap | `minimax/minimax-m3.1-flash` | CN | 0.15 | 0.60 | 0.0008 | 13 |
| Cheap | `z-ai/glm-5.3` | CN | 0.07 | 1.40 | 0.0009 | 49 |
| Mid | `google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite` | US | 0.30 | 2.50 | 0.002 | 8 |
| Mid | `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro-0813` | CN | 0.66 | 1.98 | 0.003 | 25 |
| Mid | `google/gemini-3.8-flash` | US | 0.83 | 4.13 | 0.005 | 7 |
| Mid | `openai/gpt-6.1-terra` | US | 1 | 5 | 0.006 | 4 |
| Top | `qwen/qwen3.8-max-0902` | CN | 2 | 6 | 0.009 | 2 |
| Top | `google/gemini-4-argon` | US | 2 | 10 | 0.011 | 6 |
| Top | `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5` | US | 2 | 10 | 0.011 | 8 |
| Top | `moonshotai/kimi-k3.1-pro` | CN | 2 | 10 | 0.011 | 2 |

Notes:
- Every model listed supports `structured_outputs` on at least some providers (`z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`: 32 of 38). `z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx` and `z-ai/glm-5.3-prime` were excluded because they don't support it.
- Open-weight models are served by many providers with different quantization, so quality and latency depend on who serves the call. Pinning a provider trades away automatic fallback.
- OpenRouter's API returns `latency_last_30m: null`, so there is no speed data up front.
- Most of these models were released after the planning model's training data. Choosing from this table alone would be choosing by brand and price.

## Decision

`scripts/bakeoff.ts` runs the same requests against 9 models:

`z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`, `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `qwen/qwen3.8-flash`, `google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite`, `google/gemini-3.8-flash`, `google/gemini-4-argon`, `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5`, `openai/gpt-6.1-terra`, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`.

- **Requests:** the 4 Quick actions on fixed Targets of the sample Document, plus 1 Review pass.
- **Measured:** latency, cost, schema validity and retries, plus the outputs side by side. Written to `docs/chiri/bakeoff.md`.
- **Choice:** the maintainer picks by reading the outputs. Tie-breakers, in order: Target-request latency under ~3 s, then cost. The result may be two models: a fast one for Target requests and a strong one for the Review pass.
- **Default:** configurable via `OPENROUTER_MODEL`.
- **Budget:** under US$0.50.

## Consequences

- The choice rests on evidence, not on a guess.
- About 30–40 minutes of work, plus a Gate.
- The Bake-off also verifies the `Output.object` risk from [0009](0009-ai-sdk-v7.md).

# Bake-off

Run on 2026-10-28 by `pnpm bakeoff`, which uses the same client and prompts as the app ([ADR 0010](adr/0010-model-bakeoff.md)).

- Input: the sample Document; 4 Quick actions on fixed Targets plus 1 Review pass without Focus.
- Settings for every model: strict JSON schema, `provider.require_parameters: true`, reasoning effort `low`, 30 s timeout for Target requests and 60 s for the Review pass, one silent retry on invalid output, models called one after another.
- The sample Document is English, so a Rationale in another language is a slip of the model (rule 5 of [ADR 0006](adr/0006-context-and-prompt-rules.md)). "Rationale not in English" is a heuristic count, read the outputs to confirm.
- Latencies are client wall time per request, including the silent retry when there was one. Cost comes from the OpenRouter `usage.cost` of each call.

### Why three runs

1. **Run 1.** The Rationale rule said "the language of the text you receive, not the language of these rules". Four models (GLM, DeepSeek, both small Gemini) answered in French, German or Spanish on an English Document, probably because the negative wording pushes a model away from English.

# Slice 2 verification: model client and Bake-off

Issue [#2](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/issues/2). This slice has no UI, so the checks are a captured request body, one call through the Vite proxy from a real browser, and the Bake-off.

## Strict structured output: confirmed

`@openrouter/ai-sdk-provider@3.1.0` sends a strict JSON schema for both `Output.object` and `Output.array`, so the fallback `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` is not needed and [ADR 0009](../adr/0009-ai-sdk-v7.md) stands.

The tests in `src/ai/client.test.ts` inject a `fetch` that captures the request body (no network). A Target request (`Output.object` with `suggestionSchema`) sends:

```json
{
  "model": "vendor/model-a",
  "response_format": {
    "type": "json_schema",
    "json_schema": {
      "schema": {
        "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "replacement": { "type": "string", "description": "The new text that replaces the Target, in Markdown." },
          "rationale": { "type": "string", "description": "One short sentence explaining the change, in the same language as the replacement." }
        },
        "required": ["replacement", "rationale"],
        "additionalProperties": false
      },
      "strict": true,
      "name": "response"
    }
  },
  "messages": [{ "role": "system", "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "…" }] }, { "role": "user", "content": "…" }],
  "reasoning": { "effort": "low" },
  "provider": { "require_parameters": true }
}
```

The Review pass (`Output.array` + `streamText`) sends the same envelope with `"stream": true` and this schema. The SDK owns the array wrapper, so the wire shape is `{ "elements": [...] }`, not the `{ "edits": [...] }` of [ADR 0002](../adr/0002-structured-output-app-owned-anchors.md):

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "elements": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": { "blockId": { "type": "string" }, "replacement": { "type": "string" }, "rationale": { "type": "string" } },
        "required": ["blockId", "replacement", "rationale"],
        "additionalProperties": false
      }
    }
  },
  "required": ["elements"],
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

Where the settings come from, read in the provider source (`dist/index.js`, `getArgs`): `provider` and `reasoning` are model settings (`provider.chat(model, { provider: { require_parameters: true }, structuredOutputs: { strict: true }, reasoning: { effort: 'low' } })`). `strict` already defaults to `true`; the client sets it anyway. The same keys also work through `providerOptions.openrouter`, which the provider spreads into the body.

## Other findings from the SDK and the API

- With `streamText`, a provider error (HTTP 402, 429, ...) does not throw from `elementStream`. The stream just ends and `output` rejects with `NoOutputGeneratedError`. The real error only arrives through the `onError` callback, so the client captures it there.
- `elementStream` emits an element when the next one starts or the output is complete, so the first Suggestion is delayed by roughly one element.
- A timeout raises a `TimeoutError` `DOMException`; the SDK does not retry it.
- `GET /generation?id=…` answers 404 for about a minute after the call (measured at 64 s). The client records the call right away from telemetry and enriches the record later, polling every 10 s after a 30 s wait.
- The top-level `reasoning` option of the AI SDK is not read by `getArgs` in this provider version (read from source, not tested); reasoning goes through the provider setting.
- All 9 Bake-off candidates accept `reasoning.effort: "low"` together with `require_parameters: true` (checked against `GET /api/v1/models`: some cannot turn reasoning off, all accept `low`).

## Browser check through the proxy

`pnpm dev` with a temporary DEV-only hook in `src/main.tsx` (not committed) that built the client with `createBrowserModelClient()`. In the page, `fetch` was wrapped to record outgoing headers, then a "Fix grammar" Target request was made on the `recieve` paragraph of the sample Document, with `agent-browser`.

- The request went to `http://localhost:5199/api/openrouter/chat/completions` with `Authorization: Bearer browser-placeholder-key`. The real key never reached the page; the proxy added it.
- The Suggestion came back valid: `replacement` "Once the canary looks healthy, you will receive a prompt…", `rationale` "Corrected the spelling of "recieve" to "receive".".
- `window.__aiCalls` got the record immediately, and about a minute later the same entry was replaced by the enriched one (`openRouter` and `generation` latencies, served model with its date suffix).
- After `pnpm build`: `grep -r "sk-or-" dist/` returns nothing, and neither does a search for the key's value.

![App with the client wired in, key present, no banner](img/2-1.png)

| browser check: Fix grammar on the recieve paragraph | deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash | deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-20260910 · Relace | 372 / 82 / 16 / 256 | 0.000051 | 1293 / 854 / 1030 | stop | valid | gen-1793193867-o7T3O9Bwhr9dn23uy3jC |

Two earlier calls of the same check targeted the wrong text (the editor only renders the visible lines) and were not recorded; they are counted in [ai-costs.md](../ai-costs.md).

## Bake-off

Final run: [bakeoff.md](../bakeoff.md), US$0.0559. It took three full runs because the Rationale wording and the Review prompt needed two fixes; the story is in the "Why three runs" section there. The whole slice cost US$0.23, see [ai-costs.md](../ai-costs.md).

input.message:
Review of PR #9 (slice 2). `pnpm test` (219/219), `pnpm biome check` and `pnpm build` all pass. Nothing called the real model. I checked the SDK claims against `node_modules/ai/src` 7.0.154 and the bundled provider `dist/index.js`. I found no blockers.

## 1. Standards

1. **nit (taste)**, `src/ai/telemetry.ts:40`: `callIdOf` casts `callId as string | undefined` without checking it; it is the only unchecked cast left in the ai layer. Fix: use `typeof callId === 'string' ? callId : undefined`.
2. **nit (taste)**, `scripts/bakeoff.ts:127`: `spec.id as QuickActionId` widens a `string`. Fix: type `RequestSpec` as a discriminated union so the `quick` variant holds `action: QuickActionId`.
3. **nit (taste)**, `src/ai/client.ts:332-413`: `reviewAttempt` relies on 9 `let` locals. This is acceptable in a generator, but it drifts from the "functional" rule. Fix: fold the counters into one immutable accumulator, like `ReviewValidationState`, or leave it as is.
4. **nit (glossary)**, `src/ai/client.ts:92-111`: the `ReviewEvent` variant `'edit'` and the type `AcceptedEdit` name what the glossary calls a Suggestion. Fix: rename to `'suggestion'`, or accept "edit" as the wire-level term ADR 0002 uses.

Everything else here is clean:
- no comments, no `any`, no classes of our own, English throughout;
- the layout matches AGENTS.md;
- the browser gets only `__HAS_OPENROUTER_KEY__` (a boolean) and a placeholder key, and Node reads `process.env`;
- tests inject `fetch` through `testing/fake-openrouter.ts`, so they never call the real model;
- the pure modules have TDD coverage.

## 2. Spec

1. **should-fix (doc/spec gap, not a code defect)**, `docs/chiri/adr/0002-structured-output-app-owned-anchors.md`: ADR 0002 and issue #2 both say `{ edits: [...] }`. On the wire it is `{ elements: [...] }` (SDK `Output.array`, `generate-text/output.ts:257`). This is only noted in the verification doc. ADRs are decisions. Fix: amend ADR 0002 with one line saying the SDK owns the wrapper key.
2. **should-fix (spec ambiguity, real behavior)**, `src/ai/client.ts:278` with the retries at `:326-329` and `:425`: the 30 s timeout is per attempt, so a request with one silent retry can take about 60 s before the error card, against "Timeout: 30 s" in ADR 0007. Fix (pick one):
   - pass a shared deadline into the second attempt (`timeoutMs - elapsed`), or
   - state "per attempt" in ADR 0007.
3. **should-fix (spec conflict in the prompt)**: three different language anchors.
   - `src/ai/prompts.ts:21-22`: `SAME_LANGUAGE` tells the model to write the Replacement in "the Document text" language, but rule 1 says the Target's language.
   - `src/ai/schemas.ts:15,30`: the Rationale description says "same language as the replacement", but rule 5 (and the glossary) say the Document's language.

   On a mixed-language Document they disagree. Fix: make `SAME_LANGUAGE` say "Replacement in the language of the Target, Rationale in the language of the Document", and make the schema descriptions match. The Bake-off shows this wording is sensitive, so re-check cheaply on one or two models.
4. **nit (spec interpretation)**, `src/ai/edits.ts:265-276`: for Target requests and Refine, a Replacement equal to the original is flagged (`unchanged: true`), not dropped. ADR 0002 says "drop". Fix: confirm slice 3 handles `unchanged` (no-op notice), or note it in ADR 0002.
5. **nit (real but harmless)**, `src/ai/telemetry.ts:163-168` with `registerTelemetry` in `ai/src/telemetry/telemetry-registry.ts:6`: registration pushes to `globalThis.AI_SDK_TELEMETRY_INTEGRATIONS` and never removes anything. The module-level guard keeps it idempotent within one module instance. A Vite HMR reload of `telemetry.ts` appends a second integration and keeps the old one forever. The old collector ignores the new request ids, so there is no wrong data, only a small leak and extra dispatch. Fix: keep the singleton on `globalThis` (e.g. a `Symbol.for` key), or ignore it as dev-only.
6. **nit (dead data)**, `src/ai/telemetry.ts:117-123`: the error message captured in `onError` is always overwritten by `error: meta.failure?.type` in `src/ai/client.ts:239`. Fix: drop it from the collector, or keep it as `errorDetail` in the record.
7. **nit (test gap)**, `src/ai/client.test.ts`: the Review pass has a 402 test but no 429 test. The code path is the same (`streamErrors[0]`), so add one case.
8. **nit (record ordering)**, `src/ai/client.ts:243-246`: `onRecord` fires when telemetry settles, up to 2 s grace later. So `__aiCalls` order can differ from call order when calls overlap. Records carry `startedAt`, so sort by it when building tables.

### Verified OK (checked in the SDK source)

- **Strict schemas:** the provider sends `json_schema` with `strict` defaulting to true (provider `dist/index.js:4300-4303`); `provider` and `reasoning` are model settings. The schemas are the single source for validation and JSON Schema. Unknown `blockId`, unchanged, empty, duplicate, occupied, code-block and over-6 edits are all dropped.
- **402/429 in the Review pass:** a provider error does not throw from `elementStream`; `output` rejects with `NoOutputGeneratedError` (`stream-text.ts:1903-1935`). The client takes the real error from `onError` (`streamErrors[0]`), so 402 and 429 do surface.
- **Retries:** `maxRetries: 1` plus our own retry does not double-bill on invalid output. The SDK retries only retryable `APICallError`s (429/5xx); our retry fires only on `invalid-output`. Worst case is 2 billed generations.
- **Timeout and abort:** `timeout.totalMs` becomes `AbortSignal.timeout`, merged into the fetch signal (`util/merge-abort-signals.ts`), so a timed-out stream really stops. The generator's `finally` aborts when the consumer stops early. The `TimeoutError` DOMException classifies as `timeout`.
- **Time to first element** is recorded per attempt (`firstElementMs` / `firstSuggestionMs`). Reasoning is `low` by default; the verification doc says all 9 candidates accept it with `require_parameters`.
- **Enrichment has no stray rejections:** `fetchGeneration` swallows its own errors, callbacks are wrapped in `safely`, and the tracked promises never reject. Records are matched by `generationId`, so they do not land in the wrong slot.
- **Polling cost:** polling runs only when `onRecordEnriched` is set, which is dev or Bake-off only. Each call can keep timers alive for up to about 4.5 min in dev; acceptable.
- **`window` access** is only in `createBrowserModelClient`, which nothing calls yet. `dev-log` takes a target object, and `client.ts` uses `performance.now()`, which exists in Node.
- **`window.__aiCalls`** is written only in dev (`browser-client.ts`).
- **Generation fetch** goes through the proxy (`/api/openrouter/generation`), and the proxy overwrites `Authorization`.
- **Block extraction:** top-level lezer nodes; a list is one Block; ids p1…pn; fenced and indented code with blank lines stay one Block. Neighbors are 2 before, 2 after, the first H1 as title and the last preceding heading as section.
- **Prompts:** all 5 rules are in `SYSTEM_PROMPT`, used by every prompt. Refine sends the original, the previous Instructions and the latest Replacement. The Review pass sends numbered Blocks, an optional Focus, the default criteria, max 6, most important first, and "never edit code blocks".
- **`bakeoff.md` and `ai-costs.md`:**
  - `bakeoff.md` has latency, cost, validity, retries and the outputs side by side for all 9 models.
  - The final run cost US$0.056, and all three full runs together about US$0.16, both under US$0.50.
  - The rows are in `ai-costs.md`.
  - The 60 s Review timeout used in the run is disclosed.

- /home/walter/Github/chiri-ai-editor/.claude/worktrees/chiri-implementation-orchestration-f3aad8/src/ai/telemetry.ts
- /home/walter/Github/chiri-ai-editor/.claude/worktrees/chiri-implementation-orchestration-f3aad8/src/ai/prompts.ts
- /home/walter/Github/chiri-ai-editor/.claude/worktrees/chiri-implementation-orchestration-f3aad8/src/ai/schemas.ts
- /home/walter/Github/chiri-ai-editor/.claude/worktrees/chiri-implementation-orchestration-f3aad8/src/ai/edits.ts
- /home/walter/Github/chiri-ai-editor/.claude/worktrees/chiri-implementation-orchestration-f3aad8/docs/chiri/adr/0002-structured-output-app-owned-anchors.md
